newsitem.title: USA: Dollar ends mixed after mark rallies against yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar ends mixed after mark rallies against yen.

text.p: The dollar hit a fresh 33-month high against a slumping Japanese yen on Monday, but fell against the German mark and other currencies amid signs Japan will likely hold interest rates at historic lows while German rates may soon rise.
Low Japanese rates help the dollar by enhancing the relative value of investments denominated in dollars, while higher German rates would hurt the dollar against the mark.
The yen fell across the board after Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party captured 239 of the 251 seats needed for a majority in weekend general elections.

The win suggested Japan would keep its official discount rate at 0.5 percent. Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita later bolstered that perception, telling a Tokyo audience his main monetary policy goal is securing an economic recovery.
Meanwhile, a report showed German M3 money supply growth slowed to 8.4 percent in September from 8.7 percent in August, a rate which analysts said should allow the Bundesbank to hold rates steady.

"Most of the interest we saw was to buy marks against yen. As a result, the dollar was a little heavy against the mark, but higher against the yen," said Thomas Arnold, chief currency dealer at Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank in New York.
The dollar ended at 112.72 yen, up from 112.57 late Friday, after reaching 112.90 yen, the highest level since 113.58 in January 1994, in early trading.

The dollar should continue to rally toward that historic peak in coming sessions, aided by robust U.S. stock and bond markets, while the yen suffers as oil-poor Japan struggles to offset inflation from a six-year high in oil prices, dealers said.
"There are a lot of things keeping the dollar well-bid against the yen," said Arnold.

In other trading, the dollar fell to 1.5352 marks from 1.5420 on Friday and also fell to 1.2632 Swiss francs from 1.2703. The British pound rose to $1.5923 from $1.5895. The dollar fell to Canadian $1.3463 from C$1.3487.
The mark hit a six-week high at 73.49 yen and most other currencies also rallied as funds flowed out of Japan.
The New Zealand dollar hit an eight-year high at $0.7140, while the Australian dollar and sterling also rallied against the yen.

"The Japanese election presented not a stumbling block, but more of a temporary pause, and now there is a lot of interest to move money out of Japan," said Seth Garrett, chief currency dealer at CS First Boston.
Against the mark, investors taking profits from a strong recent dollar rally accelerated dollar selling, dealers said.
The U.S. unit had risen nearly seven pfennigs in four weeks and some market players took an opportunity to take those handsome profits, dealers said.
"We saw some profit-taking in sterling and the dollar against the mark," Garrett said. "But I think we should find support soon and gradually resume the move back up."
